cross_stack_validation.description: Before trusting any comparison, jammi and torch were run at F32 (no bf16 anywhere) on the IDENTICAL synthetic tokens (jammi's round4_synthetic_ids, a SplitMix64/PCG generator, bit-ported to Python in torch_round6_layer_dump.py -- NOT torch_finetune_step.synthetic_ids, a different LCG) and the IDENTICAL shared Gaussian LoRA weights. Two independent stacks (candle vs torch) computing the same forward+backward should agree to f32 rounding.
cross_stack_validation.verdict: Harness validated: matches to 7 significant figures at both smoke and production shape, on two independent gradient axes (full trainable-weight vector AND per-layer activation-gradient boundary). Every comparison below rests on this validated base.

E4_headline_full_trainable_gradient_cosi.description: cosine of the FULL 224-tensor (7,196,672-param) concatenated trainable LoRA-gradient vector (dL/dA, dL/dB for every layer x {Wqkv,Wo,Wi,mlp.Wo}), one forward+backward, NO optimizer step. vacuous_tensor_count=0 in every comparison below (Gaussian init keeps dL/dA live, unlike round 4/5's ZerosB legs).

dispatch_confirmation.block_eager_run: every *_fused_dispatches=0, every *_eager_dispatches nonzero (ln=57, rope=56, softmax=28, geglu=28, lora_linear=112, attention_block=28)
dispatch_confirmation.flash_run: run under JAMMI_KERNELS_STRICT=1, nothing disabled; guide 3.5 zero-dispatch-is-RED confirmation: disabling ONLY attention_block_fused under the SAME flash binary reproduced the IDENTICAL loss (0.28515625) with kernels_disabled_fired=[] -- attention_block_fused was never reached, so attention_block_flash is what dispatched for all 28 layers

E4_headline_full_trainable_gradient_cosi.headline_finding: On the metric that actually drives the optimizer update (the WEIGHT-gradient direction), jammi's PRODUCTION DEFAULT bf16 arm (block-fused) has the WORST agreement with jammi's own f32 truth (cos=0.610) of the three bf16 arms measured -- worse than jammi's flash arm (0.790, almost exactly at torch's own inherent bf16 noise ceiling of 0.796) and worse than jammi's fully-decomposed eager arm (0.810, which slightly exceeds torch's own bf16 ceiling). jammi_f32 vs torch_f32 = 0.9999999 confirms jammi_f32 and torch_f32 are the SAME ground truth to within f32 rounding, so torch_eager_vs_torch_f32 (0.796) is a valid, independent calibration of 'ordinary bf16 noise at this scale' -- block-fused sits clearly BELOW that calibration; flash and eager sit AT or slightly ABOVE it.

E3_per_layer_activation_gradient_boundar.description: boundary.{1..28} = dL/d(output of encoder layer i), captured via jammi's GradTap (activation_capture::tap_boundary, existing round-4 instrumentation) and via torch's register_full_backward_hook on model.base_model.model.layers[i-1] (torch_round6_layer_dump.py, new this round). Noise calibration = torch_eager_bf16 vs torch_f32 at the SAME boundary (torch's own inherent bf16 ceiling, independent of jammi entirely).
E3_per_layer_activation_gradient_boundar.note_on_reversal_from_round5: Round 5's E2 (ZerosB init, dL/dA structurally zero) found fused BEST (0.636) and flash BEST OF ALL (0.750) on this same boundary[1-18] metric, eager WORST (0.303). Round 6 (Gaussian init, both A and B live) finds the OPPOSITE ranking: eager BEST (0.662), fused WORSE (0.445), flash WORST (0.308). This reversal is itself a measurement, not noise -- re-confirmed via the dispatch-counter check above (flash's fired path did not change) and is consistent across boundary/qkv/mlp_input alike. The LoRA init regime materially changes which arm looks best on the per-layer ACTIVATION-gradient axis.

first_departing_layer_backward_order.flash: boundary.13 (backward order, first CLEAR/sustained crossing below the same-layer torch noise floor: flash=0.5527 vs floor=0.5798; the gap then widens monotonically -- boundary.8 flash=0.425 vs floor=0.531, boundary.1-7 flash effectively UNCORRELATED with torch-eager, cos in [-0.002, 0.17])
first_departing_layer_backward_order.block_eager: no large, sustained departure -- tracks the noise floor within a few hundredths at every layer (sometimes marginally above, sometimes marginally below); the fully-decomposed candle_nn::ops::softmax path (all-native-bf16, no F32 anywhere) diverges from torch-eager no more than torch's OWN bf16 diverges from ITS OWN f32 truth
first_departing_layer_backward_order.block_fused: never departs below the noise floor at any layer -- stays 0.15-0.35 ABOVE the calibration at every single boundary. Read as a measurement, not a virtue: this is HIGHER agreement with torch-eager-bf16 than torch's own bf16 arm has with ITS OWN f32 truth, which is the signature of a SHARED, CORRELATED rounding pattern between jammi-fused and torch-eager (both bf16, both diverging from f32 truth in a similar direction) rather than evidence that jammi-fused's ACTIVATION gradients are more correct -- E4's weight-gradient axis shows fused is the worst arm vs f32 truth, so 'agrees more with torch-eager on activation gradients' and 'agrees with f32 truth on weight gradients' are NOT the same claim.

E5_sublayer_bisect.description: 8 sub-layer points per HF ModernBertEncoderLayer.forward's actual structure (transformers 5.15.1, read on this box): attn_norm -> attn(Wqkv->RoPE->scores->softmax->PV->Wo) -> resid1 -> mlp_norm -> Wi -> GeGLU(act(input)*gate) -> Wo -> resid2. Captured on torch (both eager-bf16 and f32) via a monkeypatched ModernBertEncoderLayer.forward/ModernBertMLP.forward (torch_round6_layer_dump.py --sublayer) that calls tensor.register_hook on each intermediate; self-consistency-checked against the module-level register_full_backward_hook capture (sublayer.i.resid2 vs boundary.i, exact bit match, max|delta|=0.0, at layers 1/2/28).
E5_sublayer_bisect.jammi_side_coverage: PARTIAL -- only 2 of 8 points map onto jammi's EXISTING round-4 GradTap: qkv.i = dL/d(Wqkv output), i.e. BEFORE RoPE/attention entirely (no exact torch sublayer analog captured this round); mlp_input.i = dL/d(resid1) -- an EXACT match to torch's sublayer.{i+1}.resid1. Extending jammi's own GradTap to the remaining 6 points (attn_norm, attn_out, mlp_norm, wi, geglu, wo) was NOT built this round -- see blockers.
E5_sublayer_bisect.jammi_mlp_input_vs_torch_resid1_direct_c: cos in [0.72, 0.86] for layers 0-18 (0-indexed jammi / 1-28 torch), rising to [0.96, 0.99] for layers 19-27 -- same shape and magnitude as the boundary table's fused-vs-torch-eager row, confirming the boundary-level finding is not an artifact of that one specific tap.

torch_own_within_layer_noise_signature_b.description: torch's OWN bf16-vs-f32 gradient cosine at each of the 8 sub-layer sites, per layer -- pure torch noise calibration, no jammi involved. Selected layers (grad, i.e. backward-execution order runs resid2 -> wo -> geglu -> wi -> mlp_norm -> resid1 -> attn_out -> attn_norm within a layer):
torch_own_within_layer_noise_signature_b.observation: at every deep layer checked (14, 18, 20, 28), attn_norm's OWN gradient cosine (requiring backward to have propagated through the WHOLE attention submodule -- Wo, PV, softmax, scores, RoPE, Wqkv) is consistently the HIGHEST of the 8 sites, not the lowest -- more backward propagation through this residual-heavy submodule does not monotonically add noise. The MLP sub-path (mlp_norm/wi/geglu, no residual of its own) is consistently the noisiest of the 8 sites at every layer checked. Stated as a measurement: within-layer noise accumulation is NOT simply 'more ops = more noise' at this checkpoint.

upcast_scores_diagnostic.knob_is_live: loss changes under the knob (block-eager arm, b4-s128): 471218.88 (off) -> 471834.3 (on) -- not a no-op
upcast_scores_diagnostic.finding: Under round 6's Gaussian LoRA weights, the SAME upcast-scores knob that improved round 5's ZerosB-init 'shared' arm (0.354->0.592 vs jammi f32 truth) makes jammi's block-eager arm SLIGHTLY WORSE (0.662->0.585 vs jammi f32 truth; 0.576->0.555 vs torch-eager) at this shape/seed. The knob's effect is NOT robustly beneficial across init regimes -- round 5's finding was measured entirely under ZerosB (dL/dA structurally zero), and does not reproduce once dL/dA is live. This is exactly the 'diagnose the structure, do not trust one measurement regime' lesson: the ZerosB legs answered a narrower question (dL/dB agreement only) than they were read as answering.

disable_attention_block_fused_at_the_dep.result: loss unchanged (0.28515625 == 0.28515625), kernels_disabled_fired=[] -- confirms attention_block_fused was never on the flash arm's live path (attention_block_flash preempted it), so this knob has NO effect on the flash arm by construction

flash_removes_the_departure.finding: On the WEIGHT-gradient axis (E4), flash (0.790 vs jammi f32) is close to torch's own bf16 ceiling (0.796) and clearly better than block-fused (0.610) -- flash removes MOST of block-fused's weight-gradient deficit. On the ACTIVATION-gradient axis (E3 boundary table), flash is the WORST-departing arm at early/mid layers (near-zero correlation with torch-eager for boundary.1-7), the opposite ranking. Flash does not uniformly 'fix' the divergence; it trades one axis for the other.

one_paragraph_mechanism_reading: As a measurement, not a theory: jammi's PRODUCTION default bf16 training arm (block-fused) is the WORST of jammi's three bf16 arms on the metric that drives learning (dL/d(LoRA weight) cosine vs f32 truth, E4: 0.610, vs flash's 0.790 and eager's 0.810, both close to or above torch's OWN inherent bf16 ceiling of 0.796) -- this is round 6's headline, and it inverts round 5's per-layer ACTIVATION-gradient finding (measured under a ZerosB init that made dL/dA structurally zero) that fused and flash were the BEST arms. On the ACTIVATION-gradient axis measured this round (Gaussian init, dL/dA live), flash is instead the outlier: its boundary-gradient cosine to torch-eager is indistinguishable from zero for the first several layers walking backward from layer 13, while block-fused's activation gradients agree with torch-eager MORE than torch's own bf16 arm agrees with its own f32 truth (a correlated-rounding signature, not evidence of higher fidelity, since the same arm is worst on E4). The round-5 f32-logit-upcast diagnostic, which improved the ZerosB-init 'shared' arm, does not reproduce that improvement under Gaussian init -- it makes block-eager marginally worse. Two different gradient objects (weight gradients vs per-layer activation gradients) and two different LoRA-init regimes (ZerosB vs Gaussian) produce three mutually inconsistent rankings of 'which bf16 arm is closest to truth' across rounds 5 and 6; the one ranking that matters for esc-045's actual question -- does block-fused, the shipped default, learn the way torch does -- says clearly, on the metric that gates the optimizer step, that it does not, and neither flash nor plain eager share block-fused's specific deficit there.
